definition: CoQA is a large-scale dataset for building Conversational Question Answering systems.
details: CoQA is a large-scale dataset for building Conversational Question Answering systems. CoQA contains 127,000+ questions with answers collected from 8000+ conversations.

explainer.lead: CoQA is a collection of more than 127,000 questions and answers drawn from over 8,000 conversations. It gives researchers a shared resource for building systems that can answer questions while taking conversational context into account.

tiers.eli5: CoQA is like a huge stack of quiz cards, but the cards belong to conversations instead of being random questions. A later question might only make sense if you remember what was asked before. It helps computers practise keeping track of that conversation while finding answers.
tiers.practitioner: CoQA can be used to train or compare conversational question-answering systems. Preserve earlier dialogue turns when constructing model inputs, since an isolated follow-up question may be ambiguous. Its scale—over 127,000 question-answer pairs from more than 8,000 conversations—supports repeatable experiments, but does not by itself specify an evaluation metric or training setup.
tiers.paperLevel: CoQA can be represented as D = {(c_i, q_i, a_i)}, where c_i is conversational context, q_i is a question, and a_i is its collected answer. The dataset contains |D| > 127,000 question-answer instances drawn from more than 8,000 conversations. These counts characterize dataset scale rather than model performance, and no scoring function is defined here.

explainer.example: In an illustrative conversation, a system reads: “Maya moved to Lisbon for work.” It answers “Where did Maya move?” with “Lisbon,” then answers the follow-up “Why did she go there?” with “For work.” The second answer depends on remembering that “there” refers to Lisbon.

usedIn.name: Conversational question answering
usedIn.detail: Training and evaluating systems that answer questions within multi-turn conversations.

usedIn.name: Dialogue system research
usedIn.detail: Studying how earlier questions and answers affect the interpretation of later questions.

explainer.measures: CoQA provides question-answer examples for assessing whether a system can produce answers in conversational settings. Its conversational structure makes the handling of context and follow-up questions central to the task.
caveats: A large question count does not by itself indicate how well any particular system will perform.
Evaluating questions without their conversational context can make follow-ups ambiguous.
